title: Adult Sleep Duration
population: Adults; general education, not sleep-disorder treatment
context: Consensus guidance; self-reported logs cannot diagnose a disorder
definition: The AASM/SRS consensus recommends at least seven hours of sleep regularly for healthy adults. This is a population recommendation, not a personal diagnosis or a maximum.

claims.text: The AASM/SRS consensus recommends at least seven hours of sleep regularly for healthy adults. This is a population recommendation, not a personal diagnosis or a maximum.

limitations: The consensus focuses on adults aged 18–60. Individual needs vary; longer sleep can be appropriate during recovery from sleep debt or illness. Persistent concerns require a healthcare professional.
contraindications: Seek professional help for persistent sleep concerns. This page does not provide diagnosis or change medication.

title: Sleep Timing Regularity
population: Adults; general education, not sleep-disorder treatment
context: Consensus guidance; self-reported logs cannot diagnose a disorder
definition: Sleep regularity describes consistency in the timing of falling asleep and waking. The NSF panel concluded that consistent timing matters for health, safety and performance.

claims.text: Sleep regularity describes consistency in the timing of falling asleep and waking. The NSF panel concluded that consistent timing matters for health, safety and performance.

limitations: Consensus based on available evidence does not establish a universal clock time or an exact allowable variation. Catch-up sleep may help after insufficient weekday sleep; it is not proof of complete recovery.
contraindications: Seek professional help for persistent sleep concerns. This page does not provide diagnosis or change medication.

title: Static Stretching
population: Older adults addressed by the NIA 2018 educational guide
context: Source-scoped flexibility education; not a soreness or readiness intervention
definition: A held stretch maintains a gently reached position; this page describes the NIA guide’s held-stretch examples.

claims.text: The NIA guide describes gently reaching a stretching position, holding while breathing normally and relaxing before repeating; it instructs readers not to bounce.

limitations: Historical March 2018 guidance for older adults; suitability for an individual is not established.
No improvement in soreness, endurance or strength is claimed from these flexibility instructions.
The source range is 10–30 seconds per hold and 3–5 repeats per side; timer templates use its lower bounds, not a personalized optimum.
Warm-up, repositioning and relaxation durations are unspecified and not counted as zero or estimated automatically.
Source verification and machine validation; no independent human or clinical review.
contraindications: Warm up before stretching; if only stretching, the source suggests a few minutes of easy walking without an exact duration.
Stop for sharp, stabbing or joint pain. Use slow movement without bouncing and breathe normally.
Seek qualified advice when unsure of suitability, particularly following hip or back surgery.
